summary_paragraph: A man with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, COPD, chronic kidney disease, and polysubstance abuse was admitted for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, worsening dyspnea, and a syncopal episode. His heart failure exacerbation was attributed to poor medication absorption due to gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to fluid overload. He was treated with intravenous diuresis and transitioned back to oral torsemide, with improvement in respiratory status. A small deep vein thrombosis in the right lower extremity was identified, and anticoagulation was initiated with enoxaparin and warfarin. His viral gastroenteritis resolved with supportive care, and renal function stabilized. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions on medication management, weight monitoring, and follow-up for anticoagulation control.
